text: The operation, the payload, the state filter and the masking rule of the checked-fields read come from RWB-P5-E2025-CON and are never guessed; the litigation columns that receive a fact are the columns of the same name in TSD S4 T3.1 (DF-LEG-006 black_case_no, DF-LEG-007 red_case_no, DF-LEG-008 court_name, DF-LEG-009 claim_amount, DF-LEG-010 filed_date, DF-LEG-011 judgment_date, DF-LEG-012 judgment_amount and DF-LEG-026 hearing_date), with source_document_id, source_doc_version and source_table_version beside them on legal_action; filing_date maps onto filed_date because the two names differ by a suffix and the meaning is the filing date of the court filing; a field code with no column of the same name is counted and not mapped; the type-table version stamped on the row is the tableVersion of the answer the facts were written from; and no party name is stored at all.
why: No source names the litigation-side read across the service boundary, gives legal_action or hearing a provenance column, or settles the litigation-side masking rule, while R-UNI-38 and CTL-08 require the version in force with the value; leaving them blank would make the story unbuildable and inventing a business value or a second amount column would be worse.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 4, 11, 12, 13 and 19; TSD S4 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2; FSD S4 A2.4.3.1, A2.16.3.1; RWB-P5-E2025-CON sections 11 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 41; context pack S4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11
confirm: The rwb-document contract owner publishes the operation and the masking rule, and the rwb-litigation data owner approves the source-stamp columns in the DDL, at the wave 2 contract freeze
impact: Medium: a change in the column set or the mapping is one migration and one criterion, and no rewrite of the story.

text: This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-025: the classification, the extraction, the evaluation runner, the review queue and the eleven legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC11 stay with RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the shapes, the path, the state filter and the fakes of the reader are RWB-P5-E2025-CON's, the treatment half of the same key is RWB-S2-E2025-APP's, and the two requirements of the plan's list that the legacy key puts out of scope (REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018) are answered by the document hub and tested by no criterion here. This story writes eight criteria of its own.
why: One legacy capability cannot have two owners of the same criteria; the work package carries the key as Split (rework) with an empty acs list for this story, and the same eleven criteria cannot be owned by P5, S2 and S4 at once.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 1 to 19, its section 7 acceptance criteria and its section 19 out-of-scope list; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7; work package B2-S4-022 story line for RWB-S4-E2025-APP
applied_in: Sections 1, 7, 16 and 18; fragment acs, tcs and reqs
confirm: The P5 slice owner confirms that RWB-P5-E2025-APP carries the eleven legacy criteria word for word with their origin tags
impact: Low: the split follows the ownership map and the work package.

text: No personal data is written, logged or put on a payload by this story: the row, the log lines and any message carry the case ID, the legal-action ID, the document ID and version, the type-table version, field codes, amounts and dates only. party_names is returned masked by the hub, is never mapped onto a column of rwb_litigation, and a property test fails the build if a party name reaches a row, a log line or a span attribute.
why: The guardrail of Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17 and the legacy guardrail forbid personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs, and the legacy authority note grants unmasked values to SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT only, so this service must hold none; S4 has no party or customer column in TSD S4 T3.1 in any case.
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 12, 17 and BR7; CTL-11 and DL26; TSD S4 T3.1
confirm: The privacy owner confirms the field set of the legal-action read and of any message the apply sends
impact: Low: the payload is narrower than the sources allow.

text: The outbox and inbox library, the parameters and reference-data client libraries, the workflow kit and the gateway-bff composite route are platform wave-0 and shared-library deliverables the service template already carries: they stand in no build row of this story, the metadata keeps Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E2025-CON only, and the story builds against their fakes until they publish. The case read of rwb-case is consumed and faked and is named in no C row of the plan.
why: The pattern table adds five H rows and two C rows for DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 while the work package's build list is empty and its only contract is the P5 one; every added row is a platform library or a contract the template or another service already publishes, and inventing H rows would change the build sequence of lane L-S4-A.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; Architecture v5 slides 4 and 8; work package B2-S4-022 story line for RWB-S4-E2025-APP
confirm: The platform template owner confirms the library delivery ahead of wave 2
impact: Medium: a late library delays the story, but no H row is invented in its build list.

text: The applied facts reach SCR-19 Litigation workspace through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the legal-action read of this service, one hop each, read only; the route specification, the screen field list and the layout belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners, and the hub screens SCR-30 and SCR-31 are shown read only through the same route. SCR-19 is listed first in E5, later than this story's wave 2, so the read model is proved against the route fake.
why: DP-19 replaces the monolith screen with a composite route, and no source publishes the route or the field list of the litigation screens in this wave; the legacy screen rows SCR-30 and SCR-31 are the document hub's.

text: This slice publishes no event and registers no Schedule, and both rows stay in the pattern list as prohibitions. DP-09 is used only through the outbox and inbox library for the idempotency and inbox tables of rwb_litigation and the one apply key of BR6: the hub's extraction event rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1 is rwb-document's and rwb-case's, the service has no event in the ownership map, and no DocumentFieldsApplied event is invented. DP-10 registers nothing: the intake Schedule JOB-12 is rwb-document's, and the litigation timers belong to the stage stories that run LitigationWorkflow, which this slice names and does not change.
why: Declaring a producer for an event no source assigns would put an outbox row into a slice that owns no event, and declaring a Schedule would add a job no source places in this capability; carrying both as prohibitions keeps the pattern list intact and makes the reading visible.
read: TSD S4 T5.3 (events: none); context pack S4 (events 0, jobs 0, workflow LitigationWorkflow); RWB-P5-E2025-CON section 12.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 4, 12 and 13
applied_in: Sections 1, 3, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.6, 13 and 17; fragment events_published, events_consumed and workflows
confirm: The event catalogue owner confirms that no event and no Schedule is assigned to the litigation-side document-fact fill
impact: Low: no event and no Schedule means no catalogue change and no chart change.

text: An extracted hearing_date is applied as one hearing row per legal action and date: it creates a hearing with is_active true and hearing_type left empty when the action holds none for that date, and it updates only next_date of the open hearing when one exists; a legal action in CLOSED or WITHDRAWN status accepts no fact and answers 409. The apply sets no LOV-LEGAL-STATUS value, moves no case status and satisfies no rule of the litigation state machine by itself: R-LIT-16 verifies the pack and R-LIT-44 records the judgment on their own stories.
why: TSD S4 makes legal_action_id and hearing_date required on hearing and draws hearing_type from LOV-HEARING without a default, and its state machine is driven by named events that include no document event, so a rule is needed and no source gives one; writing a hearing_type or a status value of the story's own choosing would be inventing a business value.
read: TSD S4 T3.1, T3.2, T3.3 and T4; FSD S4 A2.11 and A2.16; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 13 and AC9; context pack S4
confirm: The litigation business analyst and the S4 hearing story owner confirm the hearing_type policy and the closed-action refusal before the hearing story freezes its shape
impact: Medium: a different hearing policy is one service method and one criterion, and no other part of the story.
